learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the core problem of scarcity and choice, and explore how individuals and societies decide to allocate limited resources.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Human wants are unlimited, but the resources to satisfy them are limited (scarce). This fundamental scarcity forces us to make choices about how to best use our resources.
Every society faces three basic questions: 1. What to produce? (Guns or butter?) 2. How to produce? (More labor or more machines?) 3. For whom to produce? (Who gets to consume the goods?)

A curve showing all the maximum combinations of two goods an economy can produce given its resources and technology. It slopes downward because to produce more of one good, you must sacrifice some of the other.
The value of the next best alternative that is given up when making a choice. If you choose to study instead of watching a movie, the movie is your opportunity cost.

fun_activity.title: 🍕 The Friday Night Choice
fun_activity.instructions: You have ₹500 and two hours of free time on Friday. You can either buy a pizza and watch Netflix, OR buy a book and study. You choose the pizza. The book and the study session is your exact 'Opportunity Cost'. Every choice has a hidden price!

exam_tips: 📌 The PPF is concave to the origin because of increasing Marginal Opportunity Cost (MOC). Resources are not perfectly adaptable to producing all goods.
📌 Positive economics deals with 'what is' (facts), while normative economics deals with 'what ought to be' (opinions and judgments). Know the difference!
📌 Any point inside the PPF indicates underutilization or inefficiency of resources.
quick_recap: ⭐ The economic problem arises due to unlimited wants, scarce resources, and alternative uses of those resources.
⭐ A centrally planned economy relies on the government to solve central problems, while a market economy relies on the price mechanism (demand and supply).
⭐ A rightward shift in the PPF means economic growth (more resources or better technology).
